newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG SUES SARANAC, LOCKPORT FOR $520 MLN.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG SUES SARANAC, LOCKPORT FOR $520 MLN.

text.p: New York State Electric and Gas Co said Thursday it filed suit in federal court against Saranac Power Partners LP and Lockport Energy Associates LP, seeking to reform its contracts and seeking refunds totaling $520 million.

The utility said Saranac Power is owned and operated by CalEnergy Co Inc, which has made a hostile take-over tender offer to buy 9.9 percent of the company for $24.50 a share and the rest for $27.50 a share.

The New York utility said the suit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of New York seeks the $520 million for money it allegedly overpaid Saranac and Lockport in the form of above-market prices.
The utility said its customers could end up paying $2.8 billion more than the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act permits over the lifetime of the contracts it has with Saranac and Lockport.
It added it will request the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to review the situation if the court does not order the contracts' reform and refund immediately.
NYSEG said Wednesday it asked the New York State Public Service Commission to block CalEnergy's tender offer, saying the Nebraska-based power producer doesn't have the experience to run the company.
CalEnergy Thursday called the petition a "desperate act" and said NYSEG should "stop playing games and wasting shareholder and ratepayers' dollars."

In the law suit filed Thursday, NYSEG is requesting the court declare the rates in the Saranac and Lockport agreements are illegal and violate the ceiling set by the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act. The utility also said it requested the court to modify the rates and release NYSEG from its contract obligations.

NYSEG said its agreement with Saranac requires it to pay more than triple the regulatory price ceiling for electricity and that the contract contains escalation clauses over its 15-year term, which it estimated to result in its paying 12.2 cents per kilowatt hour.
It added its contract with Lockport has similar clauses.
NYSEG said it paid Saranac $281 million above the regulatory price ceiling since June 1994 and Lockport about $239 million since October 1992.
CalEnergy spokesmen were not immediately available to comment on the suit.
CalEnergy's stock traded at 37-1/4 Thursday afternoon, down 2-1/4. NYSEG's shares hit a new 52-week high of 26-1/4 and were trading at 26-1/16 in the late afternoon, up 1/2.
